messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: SEV2 - High packet loss to SFO edge via upstream provider 'BlueRidge' (asn:64512). >20% loss observed across multiple prefixes. Auto-created incident #INC-2026-182.

oncall-jamie: acked. I'm on it. grabbing nets. assigning to @lee_netops for upstream contact.

lee_netops: looking. I can see BGP withdraws and flaps from BRIDGE-PEER (64512) to our SFO edge. fluctuations in MED and AS-PATH. traceroute shows loss starting at their ASN.

ana_sre: noted customer-facing errors: increased 5xx rates on /inference endpoints in us-west-1 (SFO). traffic shift kicking in for some routes but not uniformly.

eng_runtime: can you paste the traceroute and a bgp summary? we should decide whether to failover traffic to LAX peers.

oncall-jamie: paste below:
```
$ mtr -r -c 10 3.121.45.67
Start: 2026-03-14T21:40:34Z
HOST: sfo-edge -> 10.0.0.2
 1. 10.0.0.1 0.4%
 2. 198.32.20.1 0.4%
 3. 198.51.100.10 22.3%  <- transit BRIDGE-PEER (64512)
 4. 3.121.45.67 22.3%
```

```
$ vtysh -c 'show ip bgp summary' | grep 64512 -A2
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcv MsgSent   TblVer  InQ OutQ  Up/Down State/PfxRcd
203.0.113.5     4 64512   1024   1020  123456   0   0  00:05:12    Idle (Cleared)
```

lee_netops: confirmed. their session is flapping. I already opened an incident with BlueRidge NOC (ticket BR-34211). they're seeing partial degradation across multiple POPs. they say "investigating hardware flaps on SFO node". ETA unknown.

ana_sre: impact assessment: roughly 12% of production requests from SFO clients are failing or timing out, latency up for another ~18% due to retransmits. This is hitting bursty real-time applications. Marking potential customer impact.

maya_cs: which customers are affected? we need to notify enterprise accounts and CS alerts.

oncall-jamie: quick list from request/ingress mapping: acct-redwood-ads, acct-quiply, acct-aurora (high qps), plus a few small fintech customers routing us-west prefer SFO. I'll DM ops for contactability.

eng_runtime: mitigation options: 1) withdraw specific prefixes via BGP to force reroute to LAX peers 2) prep traffic steering via our smart-routing to prefer dedicated LAX endpoints 3) announce more-specifics to alternate peers (risky). Thoughts?

lee_netops: prefer #2 first (control-plane steering). We should also prepare #1 as a quick blunt tool if NOC can't stabilize. Withdrawing all SFO prefixes will cause a failover but may spike latency for customers that still prefer SFO.

ana_sre: agree. do #2 now. set a canary for non-critical prefixes, monitor error rate.

oncall-jamie: executing routing policy change: enabling prefer-region LAX for us-west-1 for traffic tagged as 'inference' and 'chat'. Command:
```
$ infra-cli routing update --region us-west-1 --prefer-pop LAX --services inference,chat --dry-run false
Applied policy 'prefer-lax-usw1' to 12 routes.
```

infra-bot: CONFIG-APPLY: policy prefer-lax-usw1 applied to 12 routes across sfo-edge routers. Change-id: cfg-20260314-09.

eng_runtime: rolling metrics now. ana, can you watch request error spikes and latency for the next 5 minutes? if not improving, escalate to prefix withdraw.

ana_sre: watching. within 90s we see partial improvement: errors down from 12% -> 6%, latency p95 down ~150ms for most customers, but two prefixes still showing >10% error.

lee_netops: still seeing some traffic pinned to BRIDGE-PEER via old BGP session; looks like their path selection still preferred due to our local-preference for some sessions. I'm prepping a selective withdraw for the two problematic prefixes.

oncall-jamie: go for selective withdraw. execute only on SFO-facing sessions to avoid global route churn.

lee_netops: running withdraw now:
```
bgp> neighbor 203.0.113.5 shutdown
withdrawing 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24
```

infra-bot: BGP-ACTION: neighbor 203.0.113.5 admin-shutdown executed on sfo-edge-core-2. Change-id: bgp-esc-20260314-17.

ana_sre: immediate improvement on those prefixes: errors down to ~1-2%, overall bucket now <2% impact. p95 latency back to baseline for most.

maya_cs: sending customer note to affected accounts: "We detected transient network degradation affecting SFO POPs, traffic was shifted to alternate POPs, service restored. We're monitoring. Incident ref INC-2026-182." Will mark impacted windows.

oncall-jamie: handoff: @ana_sre will take incident lead for postmortem and customer impact writeup. I'm wrapping current actions and moving to follow-up to ensure BlueRidge performs RCA.

ana_sre: taking lead. next steps: collect BGP logs, route-refresh events, timestamps of withdraws, and BlueRidge ticket details. Postmortem owner: ana_sre. Severity remains SEV2 until BR confirms root cause and routes stabilized for 24h.

lee_netops: update from BlueRidge NOC: confirmed failed line card in SFO causing BGP flap; replaced; they completed stabilization at 2026-03-14T22:01:12Z. Ticket BR-34211 updates in the incident.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-2026-182 moved to "monitoring". Duration: ~21m. Severity: SEV2 -> monitoring. Action items created: [collect-bgp-logs, schedule-postmortem, customer-comms].

maya_cs: thanks team. I'll follow up with CS notes and send targeted emails.

oncall-jamie: closing my active watch. if anything regresses, page oncall as usual. good job folks. :thumbsup:

ana_sre: filing postmortem draft and will sync with netops + eng. will include timeline, mitigations, and follow-ups (automation to failover sooner, improve BGP health monitoring).

lee_netops: saving captures and BGP dumps to s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-2026-182/.

infra-bot: ARTIFACT: logs uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-2026-182/bgp-dump.tar.gz

incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigation. Monitoring window 24h.
